summary: Ayinapalli Aiyappan studied at the University of Madras and worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1971).

Ayu Khandro was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.
Ayush Maheshwari specializes in computational studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and subsequently held a post there.

Ayya Khema was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied under teachers including Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Narada Mahathera, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Nyanarama. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and Jhana Verlag, and taught at Buddha-Haus in 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), where she has studied under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Amherst College, Stanford University (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt), and under multiple traditional teachers. He lectured at UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001) and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (2003).

B. N. Goswamy was an Indologist and art historian. He studied at Panjab University (~1950–1961), served in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958), and later held a post at Panjab University (~1965–1993).

B. N. K. Sharma was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Madras and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He held posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, Dr. A. V. Baliga College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia University, LSE, Bonn, and Gray's Inn under scholars including John Dewey and Edwin Seligman. He served as professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

B. R. Gopal was an Indologist and historian. He served as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

B. R. Sharma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Assistant Director of Research at the Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) and as a scientist at the Arid Forest Research Institute (2020), teaching Jitindera Kumar Sinha.

Baatr Kitinov works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD in World History at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University under Ralph Lilley Turner. He taught Pierre Meile and served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1968).

Baden Henry Baden-Powell worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at St Paul's School and the University of Oxford, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1889) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (~1882–1883).

Bahadur Chand Chhabra worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953) and held posts at the ASI and Panjab University.
Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University, taught Osamu Takata, and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1952), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952), and the Institute of Philosophy at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford (~1948–1952). He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1945–1976) and taught Durga Prasad Dikshit.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and taught mathematics at the New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar was an archaeologist who studied at the University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (1982–1992).
